What kind of sights will I see on the Chicago Architecture River Cruise?

If it includes candlelight, curtained booths, and live guitarists strumming flamenco on their nylon strings, you've likely already spent a night at Geja's Cafe, named #1 of USA Today's most romantic restaurants. If you haven't, picture an intimate fondue restaurant with all the ambiance of a Spanish hideaway—right down to the vintage wine bottles lining the walls. This setting could only be Geja's, a Lincoln Park institution that has traded in melted cheese and melted hearts since 1965. Here's a look at the key elements that keep couples coming back to Geja's for more.
Fine Fondue Dining.
The signature Geja's experience is the three-course Premier Dinner. To start the meal, servers fire up a cast-iron pot filled with brandy-spiked Swiss gruyere, into which diners then dip fruits, veggies and breads. A crisp green salad with dijon vinaigrette cleanses the palate for the main course: veggies and your choice of meat—perhaps lobster tail or chicken breast—cooked in sizzling vegetable oil or broth. The communal meal closes with a dessert of churros, pound cake, marshmallows, and fruit dipped in flaming belgian chocolate.
International Wine List.
Geja's Cafe has specialized in wine since opening in the mid-1960s. In fact, the restaurant claims to be the oldest wine bar in the city, and this legacy is written all over the current wine list. Servers will recommend the perfect white, red, or crisp sparkling varietal to accompany your meal; Geja's also works with the San Antonio Winery to produce its own private-label chardonnay, merlot, and cabernet sauvignon.

A half-century of memories fills this softly lit eatery on Armitage Avenue. (The restaurant was originally located on Wells Street, then moved to its current home in 1971.) Geja's has played host to literally thousands of marriage proposals over the years, earning it an enduring reputation as one of Chicago's most romantic restaurants. full_content:
These four iconic sites each offer a unique perspective on the first 20 years of Wright's architecture, emblematic of his American Prairie Style

Highlights
Immersive guided tours of Frank Lloyd Wright's groundbreaking architectural sites: Home and Studio (Oak Park), Unity Temple (Oak Park), Robie House (Hyde Park), Rookery Building (Downtown Chicago).
Insights into the Prairie style and modern architectural principles.

What to Expect

Step into the architectural legacy of Frank Lloyd Wright with the Frank Lloyd Wright Trust. Visitors can embark on captivating guided tours that delve into the genius of Wright's designs and the profound impact he had on Modern American architecture. Explore the very spaces where groundbreaking ideas were born, offering a unique glimpse into the mind of a visionary.

Each tour provides an opportunity to witness architectural masterpieces, from the Prairie style innovation of the Home and Studio and the iconic Robie House, to the dramatic interior of the Rookery Light Court and the radical spirituality of Unity Temple. Experience firsthand the beauty and innovation that led these sites to be inscribed on the World Heritage List, inspiring future generations with Wright's enduring vision.

Plan Your Visit

Operating Hours

Hours may vary. Please check the merchant's website for the most up-to-date information: https://flwright.org/tour (ACTION REQUIRED: GROUPON Voucher holders must call in advance at 312-994-4000 to reserve a specific date and time for a guided interior tour).

Please Note
After reservations are placed with the Frank Lloyd Wright Trust, tickets are not refundable or exchangeable.
Late arrivals will join their ticketed tour in progress. We recommend arriving no later than 15 minutes before the start time of your tour.
Guests must check-in at the Museum Shop before joining their tour.
We do not recommend our interior tours for children under 8 years old. All guests, regardless of age, must have a ticket. Strollers are not permitted on the tours.
For questions about site accessibility call 312-994-4000

Tour Schedule

The Frank Lloyd Wright Trust offers guided tours of Wright's Home and Studio, Robie House, Rookery Light Court, and Unity Temple. Please note the location of each site when planning your visit:

Home and Studio: 951 Chicago Ave. Oak Park, IL 60302
Unity Temple: 875 Lake Street Oak Park, IL 60301
Robie House: 5757 S Woodlawn Ave. Chicago, IL 60637
Rookery Building: 209 S LaSalle Street Chicago, IL 60604

Important Information — The Frank Lloyd Wright Trust is dedicated to engaging, educating, and inspiring the public through the interpretation and preservation of Frank Lloyd Wright's design legacy and original sites for future generations.

Ticket Options
Home and Studio Guided Interior Tour

Enjoy a guided tour of Wright's Home and explore the Studio where the first uniquely Modern American architecture - the Prairie style - was created.

Robie House: A Modern Home Guided Tour

Frank Lloyd Wright’s Robie House, completed in 1910, stands as a cornerstone of modern architecture and the most celebrated of his Prairie houses. Inspired by the Midwest landscape, its design exemplifies Wright’s vision and is inscribed on the World Heritage List.

Rookery Light Court Guided Tour

The Rookery Building, designed by Daniel Burnham and John Root in 1888, is a Chicago landmark featuring one of Frank Lloyd Wright’s most striking interiors—a luminous central light court. Wright’s 1905 remodel balanced Burnham & Root’s ornate ironwork with his own vision, creating a spectacular environment.

Unity Temple Guided Interior Tour

Unity Temple, designed in Frank Lloyd Wright’s Oak Park Studio, marks a pivotal achievement of his Prairie era. Its radical exterior, with the use of reinforced concrete, houses a new spatial concept for worship in an open and light filled sanctuary that has earned inscription on the World Heritage List. "When I finished Unity Temple, I had it. I knew I had the beginning of a great thing, a great truth in architecture." - Frank Lloyd Wright.

Ready for a dose of history? Visiting a museum offers countless benefits beyond just brushing up on facts, it's like stepping straight into another time. From interactive galleries showcasing protest art to regional cultural heritage walking tours, this isn't just about looking at old stuff; it's about really getting what shaped our world today.

Why You Should Grab The Offer

Explore the history of Chicago and the United States through permanent and temporary exhibitions, drawn from more than 20 million items in the Chicago History Museum’s collections with Museum Admission Tickets. Permanent exhibitions like "Chicago: Crossroads of America" offer a comprehensive look at the city's evolution, showcasing artifacts that range from the original Fort Dearborn chunk to the first locomotive in Chicago. Temporary exhibitions rotate regularly, featuring photography, documents, and interviews that enrich the narrative of Chicago's dynamic past, ensuring there's always something new to discover with each visit. With a 4.7 rating on Groupon, the Chicago History Museum offers a highly recommended journey through the city's vibrant past and pivotal contributions to American history.




Chicago History Museum Highlights

Chicago: Crossroads of America - Learn what makes Chicago home sweet home. Explore the city's history through a series of themed galleries that highlight artifacts through interactive features and multimedia presentations.

Sensing Chicago - This multi-sensory experience includes hopping on a high-wheel bicycle, hearing the Great Chicago Fire, catching a fly ball at Comiskey Park, smelling the Union Stock Yard, and diving into a giant Chicago-style hot dog.

Abraham Lincoln - In this installation, you’ll learn all about former president Abraham Lincoln, his leadership during the Civil War, and his assassination.

Facing Freedom in America - Examine the stories behind eight conflicts over American freedom dating from the 1850s to the 1970s. This exhibition uses artifacts, images, and interactive displays to explore everything from women’s suffrage to Japanese internment.

Jaffee History Trail - This outdoor, interpretive path incorporates features such as a native species garden, the Couch Tomb, and a 13,000-pound, metal relic from the 1871 Great Chicago Fire.


The Great Chicago Adventure - In the dynamic film presentation, “The Great Chicago Adventure,” experience the intensity of the Great Chicago Fire and splendor of the World’s Columbian Exposition, explore the sights of bustling Maxwell Street in the 1950s, and peer down from an I-beam at the top of the Sears Tower in the 1970s.

full_content:
Discover a full day of hands-on fun at Liberty Science Center! Explore 12 interactive exhibit halls, meet 110+ animal species, dig for dinosaur fossils, tackle the iconic Touch Tunnel, and enjoy the Western Hemisphere’s largest planetarium. Perfect for curious minds of all ages!

Highlights

Access to 12 museum exhibition halls and permanent engaging exhibits like Touch Tunnel and Microbes Rule!

Upgrade your experience with a visit to the Jennifer Chalsty Planetarium, the Western Hemisphere's biggest planetarium. (planetarium admission sold separately)

Opportunities to interact with live animals, including 110 species and giant aquariums.

Hands-on learning experiences such as climbing a rock wall and digging for dinosaur fossils.

A perfect gift for families and science enthusiasts of all ages, fostering discovery and fun.

What To Expect
Step into a world of discovery at Liberty Science Center, a cutting-edge 300,000-square-foot learning and entertainment venue. Their mission is to inspire the next generation of scientists and engineers, exciting learners of all ages with the power and pure fun of science and technology. Guests can immerse themselves in 12 museum exhibition halls, encounter a diverse live animal collection with 110 species, and marvel at giant aquariums.
Prepare for hands-on interactive exhibits where visitors can test friction on a rock wall, touch live animals in the Touch Tank, or uncover ancient dinosaur fossils in the Dino Dig Adventure. Your general admission ticket grants access to all permanent exhibits halls and galleries. For an additional fee, customers can enjoy the spectacular Jennifer Chalsty Planetarium, the Western Hemisphere's biggest planetarium, offering unparalleled celestial journeys.
Plan Your Visit
Operating Hours
Hours may vary. Please check the merchant's website for the most up-to-date information.
Location
Liberty State Park, 222 Jersey City Boulevard, Jersey City, NJ 07305
Exhibitions
Thomas & Friends: Explore the Rails - Opened on May 30, 2026, this exhibition lets kids learn, play, and discover math, science, and engineering through hands‑on fun with Thomas, Percy, Victor, and friends across beloved TV locations.
Dino Dig Adventure - Uncover ancient dinosaur fossils buried in more than 60 tons of sand! In Dino Dig Adventure, you'll be immersed in the landscape of a real paleontological dig. Search for fossils from seven different dinosaur species, including replicas of bones, eggs, and even dinosaur poop.
Touch Tunnel - Liberty Science Center’s iconic 80‑foot Touch Tunnel offers an unforgettable crawl‑through adventure in pitch darkness, revealing how much we rely on sight while creating lasting memories across generations.
Infinity Climber - The world’s first suspended climbing play space, Liberty Science Center’s Infinity Climber® spans 26 feet wide, 24 feet deep, and 19 feet tall, surrounded by 19 miles of protective wire, offering multiple thrilling routes for a 21st‑century climbing adventure.
Wobbly World - Created with renowned toy designer Cas Holman, is a bright, off‑kilter wonderland where young children (42" or less in height) explore balance, motion, and cause‑and‑effect in a one‑of‑a‑kind exhibition.
Wild About Animals - Cotton-top tamarin monkeys. Red-footed tortoises. Naked mole rats! Liberty Science Center is home to 100+ fascinating animal species. Come meet many of them in our Wild About Animals exhibition.
The Great Train Set - Captures the marvels of 1950s rail travel with one of the most elaborate model railroads ever built, recreating the Lackawanna line from Hoboken Terminal through small‑town New Jersey to Pennsylvania coal country in unforgettable detail.
Universe Revealed - This gallery showcases NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope—a million miles out in space—highlighting its extraordinary engineering feats and breathtakingly detailed images of the cosmos.
Making Mammoths - On Liberty Science Center’s third floor, Making Mammoths unveils groundbreaking science led by Harvard geneticist George Church—complete with a stunning woolly mammoth replica—exploring how reviving these giants could even help combat global warming.
Microbes Rule! - Step inside Microbes Rule! to explore the mighty microscopic organisms that shape life on Earth—through stunning art and technology, discover how most microbes benefit us and are essential to our survival.
Cosmic Portal - Walk through Liberty Science Center’s Cosmic Portal, a stunning wormhole‑inspired vestibule where immersive imagery, sound, and lighting effects transport you into the compression and expansion of space and time.
Monuments to Motherhood - Unveiled May 18, 2026, Liberty Science Center’s Monuments to Motherhood by artist Molly Gochman honours caregivers across generations with intertwining cast‑bronze forms that invite hands‑on interaction and shared experience.
Our Hudson Home - The Hudson River is home to thousands of species – including our own! In Our Hudson Home, discover the importance of this river as a means of travel and commerce, a source of food, and a place to play.
Izzo Family Touch Tank - The Touch Tank allows you to safely touch horseshoe crabs, sea urchins, whelks, sea stars, and other creatures that call the Hudson their home. Don't miss this stunning new feature of Our Hudson Home!
Hoberman Sphere - At Liberty Science Center, the iconic Hoberman Sphere—designed by artist‑engineer Chuck Hoberman—expands and contracts with hundreds of scissor‑like connectors, delighting millions since 1992 and showcasing brilliant engineering in motion.
The Dream Machine - At Liberty Science Center, The Dream Machine transforms bicycle pumps into bursts of colour, sound, and scent—an interactive sensory adventure that stirs emotions from joy to disgust to hope.
Energy Quest 2.0 - In Liberty Science Center’s newly renovated Energy Quest 2.0, explore solar and wind power, race hand‑crank cars, and pedal bikes that run appliances—an interactive adventure revealing the ingenuity behind unlocking energy all around us.
Pixel Art - Unleash your creativity at Liberty Science Center’s Pixel Art wall, where 952 rotating dials with over 1,000 colour options let you design vibrant patterns and share your coolest creations online with #LibertyScienceCenter.
Wonder Why - Kids and families celebrate the joy of science through hands‑on challenges—hang from bars, climb rock walls, make minerals glow, and test your mind with optical illusions.
Bees to Bots - The third floor of Liberty Science Center is buzzing with excitement! In Bees to Bots, peer inside our honey bee hive to see real bees at work, busily building honeycomb and making honey. Then explore our multimedia exhibition to discover innovative ways that scientists are studying bees.
Brain Games - Practice your critical thinking skills and challenge yourself! In Brain Games, you’ll discover coding by teaching a robot to navigate a maze, piece together magnet shapes to create the five Platonic Solids, explore patterns using big colorful foam blocks, and more.

deal_title: Savor Historic Diner Dishes: $20 or $40 Voucher for Food and Drink at Mel's Drive-In. Save Up to 38%
merchant_info:
In 1947, owners Mel Weiss and Harold Dobbs assembled a staff of 14 carhops to serve passing motorists at the first Mel's Drive-In. For the next two decades, customers partial to automobile dining flocked to the chain’s 11 California locations, eager to wash down grass-fed half-pound burgers with thick milk shakes. As fast-food outlets outpaced the drive-in's once-speedy service, its popularity declined, and it was eventually scheduled for demolition. The building got a temporary reprieve, however, when filmmaker George Lucas decided to use the drive-in's original location on Lombard Street as the colorful backdrop for his film American Graffiti. As bulldozers destroyed the last remnants of the historic drive-in, American Graffiti opened in theaters.
A decade later, though, Mel's son Steven reopened Mel's Drive-In in an attempt to carry on his father's dream. Steven restored the drive-in's multiple locations to mirror their original motif by stocking each with midcentury must-haves such as illuminated marquees, jukeboxes, and Elvis-themed WiFi passwords. The drive-in’s menu, meanwhile, balances period-appropriate fare, such as hot dogs and burgers, with healthy options, such as the Haven’s Famous vegetarian sandwich, two slices of nine-grain bread topped with avocado, sprouts, and tomatoes.
